name: Face X-Ray Boundary
description: Detects blending boundaries using Face X-Ray technique (Li et al., 2020)
algorithm: Face X-Ray Boundary — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method implements the Face X-ray technique from Li et al. (2020) for general face forgery detection:

1. **Blending Boundary Hypothesis**: Face X-ray is based on the key insight that most face manipulation methods share a common step — blending a modified face region onto a background. This blending creates a detectable boundary even when the face modification itself is imperceptible. The method targets this universal blending step rather than specific manipulation artifacts.

2. **Gray-Scale Blending Map Estimation**: For each pixel, the method estimates whether it belongs to a blending boundary. The "face X-ray" is computed as a map B(x) indicating the probability that pixel x is at a face blending boundary. This is estimated using the observation that blended regions show HR (high-resolution) content from the face source mixed with LR (low-resolution) content from the background at boundaries.

3. **Multi-Scale Boundary Detection**: The face X-ray is computed at multiple scales to detect blending at different resolutions. Blending boundaries may be sharp (simple alpha compositing) or smooth (Poisson blending, feathered masks), requiring multi-scale analysis for robust detection.

4. **Cross-Color-Space Analysis**: The blending boundary signature is analyzed in multiple color spaces (RGB, YCbCr, HSV). Different color channels may show blending artifacts with varying intensity — YCbCr chrominance channels are particularly sensitive to blending artifacts that are invisible in luminance.

5. **Temporal X-ray Consistency**: The face X-ray map is computed per frame and tracked temporally. A persistent blending boundary at consistent facial locations across frames provides strong evidence of face manipulation. The temporal stability of the X-ray signal increases detection confidence and reduces false positives from compression artifacts or natural skin boundaries.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through face x-ray boundary analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Li, Y. et al. (2020). Face X-ray for More General Face Forgery Detection. CVPR.
Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
